name: Connecting Ridge
elevationProduct: PGDA LOLA 5 m site map Site01
note: Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. The point with the most sunlight 2 m above the ground at the south pole (cluster C1). Artemis III candidate region in NASA's 2022 list.
source: Gläser et al. 2018, Planetary and Space Science 162, 170-178, Table 2 (2 m above ground), Connecting Ridge C1 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20170007365)
frameEvidence: Gläser et al. 2018 state no frame; their terrain model is LOLA tracks (MOON_ME of DE421) co-registered to an LROC NAC terrain model. Check: on NASA's MOON_ME DE421 5 m maps this exact point gets 86.1% sunlight 2 m up against Gläser's 88.0%, while points 100 m away get a median of 65.9%, so the point agrees with MOON_ME_DE421 to well under 100 m.
summary: Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters with the most sunlight 2 m above the ground at the south pole.

name: Connecting Ridge Extension
elevationProduct: PGDA LOLA 5 m site map SL3
note: Second high-sunlight cluster on the same ridge (C2), further from Shackleton. Artemis III candidate region in NASA's 2022 list.
source: Gläser et al. 2018, Planetary and Space Science 162, 170-178, Table 2 (2 m above ground), Connecting Ridge C2 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20170007365)
frameEvidence: Gläser et al. 2018 state no frame; their terrain model is LOLA tracks (MOON_ME of DE421) co-registered to an LROC NAC terrain model. Check: on NASA's MOON_ME DE421 5 m maps this exact point gets 78.7% sunlight 2 m up against Gläser's 78.1%, while points 100 m away get a median of 50.7%, so the point agrees with MOON_ME_DE421 to well under 100 m.
summary: Second sunlit stretch of the same ridge, further from Shackleton crater.

name: Shackleton rim
elevationProduct: PGDA LOLA 5 m site map Site04
note: Rim of Shackleton crater, almost on the pole. The better of the two rim points listed 2 m above the ground. Not a named Artemis III region.
source: Gläser et al. 2018, Planetary and Space Science 162, 170-178, Table 2 (2 m above ground), Shackleton, first row (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20170007365)
frameEvidence: Gläser et al. 2018 state no frame; their terrain model is LOLA tracks (MOON_ME of DE421) co-registered to an LROC NAC terrain model. Check: on NASA's MOON_ME DE421 5 m maps this exact point gets 84.2% sunlight 2 m up against Gläser's 85.5%, while points 100 m away get a median of 53.0%, so the point agrees with MOON_ME_DE421 to well under 100 m.
summary: Rim of Shackleton crater about 10 km from the south pole, in sunlight most of the time.

name: Peak near Shackleton
elevationProduct: PGDA LOLA 5 m site map Site07
note: Isolated peak on the far side of Shackleton (Site 7). Artemis III candidate region in NASA's 2022 list. Spot derived by us: the sunniest point 2 m above the ground within 2 km of the published region centre, on a slope under 10° over 100 m.
source: Derived with science/best_spot.py from NASA PGDA 5 m LOLA terrain (https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78). Region centre: De Rosa et al. 2012, Planetary and Space Science 74, 224-246, Table 2, Shackleton Vicinity SV1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.5587)
frameEvidence: Picked on NASA PGDA 5 m maps, stated by PGDA and Barker et al. 2021 to be in the MOON_ME frame of DE421; the region centre (De Rosa et al. 2012, Table 2) is stated as ME/PA, DE421.
summary: Isolated peak on the far side of Shackleton crater, named an Artemis landing region in 2022.

name: de Gerlache rim

frameEvidence: Picked on NASA PGDA 5 m maps, stated by PGDA and Barker et al. 2021 to be in the MOON_ME frame of DE421; the region centre (De Rosa et al. 2012, Table 2) is stated as ME/PA, DE421.

name: Apollo 11
note: Tranquility Base, 20 July 1969. Equatorial contrast: the Sun rises and sets once a month, high in the sky. Horizon is a smooth sphere.

frameEvidence: LROC states the mean Earth/polar axis (ME) system; DE421 is the ME realization the LRO project uses (Barker et al. 2021).
summary: First crewed Moon landing, in Mare Tranquillitatis.
